# Task 9 — access requests (backend)

Visitor onboarding: `pending -> approved -> activated`; terminal `rejected`, `expired`. Contract: playbook §8.1.
Simulation-only project: nothing here touches a real facility; accounts created are `viewer` accounts.

## Variables

| Variable | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `ACCESS_REQUESTS_ENABLED` | `true` | `false`/`0`/`no`/`off` makes every route below answer 404. |
| `ACCESS_PUBLIC_BASE_URL` | unset | Origin used to build `<base>/activate#token=...`. Unset: `http://localhost:5173` outside production; in production no link can be built, so the activation mail is recorded as `not_configured` (`no_base_url`). |
| `ACCESS_TOKEN_PEPPER` (or `ACCESS_TOKEN_PEPPER_FILE`) | dev default | HMAC key for token hashes and IP hashes. **Required in production:** `setup()` raises and the plugin loader skips the whole plugin (ERROR log) rather than serving routes keyed with a public default. In development a public default is used with one warning. Rotating it invalidates every outstanding status/activation token. |
| `ACCESS_REQUEST_TTL_DAYS` | `7` | A pending request expires after this long. |
| `ACCESS_ACTIVATION_TTL_HOURS` | `24` | Life of one activation link. |
| `ACCESS_NOTIFY_OWNER_EMAIL` | unset | Recipient of the "new request" mail. Unset: recorded as `not_configured` (`no_owner_email`). |

Mail itself (`ACCESS_NOTIFY_BACKEND`, SMTP settings) belongs to Task 10 (`src/notify/mail.py`). Until that module exists the
service records `notify_state=not_configured`, `notify_last_code=mail_unavailable`; requests, decisions and activation work.

## Routes

Public: `POST /api/access-requests` (5/h per IP, 3/24 h per email), `GET /api/access-requests/{ref}/status` (60/min per IP,
header `X-Request-Token`), `POST /api/access-requests/resend-activation` (3/h per IP; also 3/h per request), `POST /api/access-requests/activate` (10/h per IP).
Admin (`require_admin`): `GET /api/admin/access-requests[?status=&limit=&before_id=]`, `GET .../{id}`, `POST .../{id}/approve|reject|resend-notification|resend-activation`.
Limits are in-memory per process and follow the shared switches (`limiter.enabled`, `HTTP_LIMITS_ENABLED`).

## Behaviour worth knowing

* Tokens are 32 random bytes (43 chars); only `HMAC-SHA256(pepper, token)` is stored. Client IPs are stored as an HMAC too.
* A submission for an address that already has an account, or an approved request, creates **no row** and returns a
  decoy `ref`/`status_token` that polls as `pending` (then `expired`) — see `src/access/tokens.py`.
* A duplicate pending submission returns the existing `ref` and rotates the status token (the previous token stops working).
* Expiry is lazy and applies to `pending` requests; an `approved` request stays approved until activated.
* Activation creates `User(username=<normalised email>, role="viewer")` and issues no session; the visitor signs in at `/auth/login`.
* Audit rows (`access_request_*`) hold the request id and ref and result codes only — no token, password, address or IP.
  `access_request_activation_failed` and `access_request_notify_failed` are best-effort (they survive a rollback).
* Mail is sent after the response (background task); a slow or broken mailer cannot delay or fail a request.
  `notify_*` columns describe the most recent mail for the request (owner notice, activation or rejection) by short code only.

## Migration

`20261101000000_access_requests` (down_revision `20261008000000`): one table, partial unique index `uq_access_one_pending`
(SQLite and PostgreSQL). `alembic upgrade head; alembic heads; alembic check`.
